page.layout: One page of text: a Latin verse dedication at the top, set in italic with the first words of some lines underlined. Below it, right-aligned, the signature "Ioh. Noviomag. Rector / S.Bud." Then a woodcut heart-shaped ornament in the centre. Bottom right, the catchword "DE".

l.i: Hoc titulus sibi vult: hoc est producere vitam.: Quam si, Mome, placet carpere: carpe nihil.
Ad te sed redeo, Phœbea qui decus ingens Artis, & Aonii gloria summa chori:
Hic tuus, ecce, liber, vitæ qui regula, quiq, Ingenio summo scriptus & eloquio:
Hic, inquam, vivat, summoq; habeatur honore, Tu quoq; Nelida secula vive senis.
Vive diu, scriptusq; bonis bene perge mereri Nominis unde tui fama perennis erit.

page.notes: The woodcut heart-shaped ornament in the centre of the page is not transcribed. The printed line "Hoc titulus sibi vult" ends with a colon-like mark after "vitam", which may be a printing error or a stop with a colon; the exact mark is uncertain. The initial "A" of "Adte" is set in a decorated form; I read it as "Ad". Punctuation at the ends of lines 1 and 3 is faint. The verse is set in italic throughout, with the names in the signature in roman type.
